look_here_first: Think tall riparian Amorpha: false indigo bush is a much larger open shrub with long pinnate leaves, many broad oval leaflets, and elongated purple flower spikes carried at the ends of upper branches.

project_inclusion.range_basis: Hays — Master Plant Pool marks the species Hays-local with multiple wild observations. Travis — UT Plant Resources Center's Travis County Fabaceae specimen index includes Amorpha fruticosa. Williamson — UT Plant Resources Center's Williamson County vascular flora includes Amorpha fruticosa.
project_inclusion.range_guardrail: Existing anchor repair only; no inferred counties.

best_field_traits: tall multi-stemmed shrub often 2–3 m or more
many relatively large oblong to oval leaflets
single banner petal with conspicuous yellow-orange stamens
moist streambanks, lake margins, and riparian thickets
morphology_keys.comparison_training: A. fruticosa is the tall riparian member of the local comparison set. A. canescens is much shorter, gray-hairy and prairie-like; A. roemeriana is a smaller limestone shrub with greener less-hairy foliage.
